chapter: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
title: A drunk demands "Honeysuckle Rose"
summary: After the flag-waver a drunk insults Hines, who answers sharply, while Budd unlatches his brother's pistol in the briefcase.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So we played. We used to play five numbers to a set. So on the ending of our set we played what we called the flag waver. That's one of these long, hot tunes, and we just build and build and build and take it out, and then we take an intermission, like a break, to pick our next set out and take a smoke in between. And that flag waver happened to be 'Honeysuckle Rose'. So when we finished 'Honeysuckle Rose',
by the time we finished it, I mean, really, the cat didn't know what we were playing. You know, I'll give him the benefit of the doubt.

So anyway, a drunken white fellow walked up to the piano where Earl was sitting, and he says, 'hey, nigger, he says, play Honeysuckle Rose.' So he came on so strongly and so abrupt and so fast and caught Earl off guard, he was like thinking of something else, and he says, 'what are you talking about?' He said, 'we just got through playing Honeysuckle Rose. If you don't know Honeysuckle Rose when you hear it, I'm sorry. Now get away from me because we have 1,500 other people here to try to entertain.' Like, I mean --

Yeah, he was, you know, like -- get away from me with this crap, man. You know? So this guy says, what? He says, you wait till I come back. Huh. We weren't thinking about anything. Well, see, I'm sitting right here, and, as I told you, I was the music director. And I'm looking down on Earl. And I said, oh, hell, you know, like I'm recognizing what's going on more so than Earl. So I had my briefcase. I had one of them old, big briefcases, and I unlatched it, and I had one of Cag's 45's -- Cag had -- I had a 38 Colt automatic on a 45 frame. It was Cag's, you know --
